egypt.fact: In 1922 Howard Carter found the golden treasures of the young pharaoh Tutankhamun in his tomb in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.
egypt.ask: In which country did Howard Carter find young King Tutankhamun's treasure-filled tomb in 1922?

egypt.fact: Cleopatra, famous for her friendships with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, more than 2,000 years ago.
egypt.ask: Which country did Queen Cleopatra rule more than 2,000 years ago?

egypt.fact: The Rosetta Stone, found in Egypt in 1799, has the same message in three scripts, which helped experts finally read Egyptian hieroglyphs.
egypt.ask: In which country was the Rosetta Stone found, the key to reading ancient hieroglyphs?

sudan.fact: About 2,700 years ago, kings of Kush from what is now Sudan conquered Egypt and ruled it as pharaohs.
sudan.ask: Which country's ancient Kushite kings once conquered Egypt and ruled it as pharaohs?

tunisia.fact: The Roman amphitheater of El Jem in Tunisia, built about 1,800 years ago, could seat about 35,000 people.
tunisia.ask: Which country's El Jem has a huge Roman amphitheater that seated about 35,000 people?

algeria.fact: Timgad in Algeria is a Roman town founded around the year 100 by Emperor Trajan, with streets laid out in a neat grid.
algeria.ask: Which country's Timgad is a Roman town founded by Emperor Trajan, with streets in a neat grid?

morocco.fact: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, was founded in 859 by a woman named Fatima al-Fihri and is often called the world's oldest university still running.
morocco.ask: Which country's al-Qarawiyyin, founded by Fatima al-Fihri in 859, may be the oldest university?

morocco.fact: Ibn Battuta, born in Tangier, Morocco, in 1304, traveled across Africa, Asia and Europe for about 30 years and wrote about his journeys.
morocco.ask: Which country was Ibn Battuta from, the explorer who traveled for about 30 years in the 1300s?

mauritania.fact: Chinguetti, an old desert trading town in Mauritania, keeps family libraries full of handwritten books hundreds of years old.
mauritania.ask: Which country's desert town of Chinguetti keeps family libraries of old handwritten books?

mali.fact: Mansa Musa, emperor of the Mali Empire in the 1300s, was famous for his gold and is often called one of the richest people who ever lived.
mali.ask: Which country shares its name with the empire of Mansa Musa, famous for its gold?

mali.fact: Sundiata Keita founded the Mali Empire in the 1230s, and his life story, the Epic of Sundiata, is still told by griots, West African storytellers.
mali.ask: Which country's name comes from the empire Sundiata Keita founded in the 1230s?

niger.fact: Agadez, in Niger, was a stop for camel caravans crossing the Sahara. Its mud-brick Grand Mosque was first built in 1515 and rebuilt in the same style in 1844.
niger.ask: Which country's desert city of Agadez has a mud-brick Grand Mosque first built in 1515?

chad.fact: The Ennedi Plateau in Chad has thousands of ancient rock paintings and carvings, including pictures of camels and cattle.
chad.ask: Which country's Ennedi Plateau has thousands of ancient rock paintings of people and animals?

nigeria.fact: The Nok people of Nigeria made clay sculptures of human heads more than 2,000 years ago.
nigeria.ask: Which country's ancient Nok people made clay sculptures of heads more than 2,000 years ago?

nigeria.fact: Artists in the ancient city of Ife, in Nigeria, made lifelike heads of bronze-like metal and clay about 700 years ago.
nigeria.ask: Which country's ancient city of Ife is famous for lifelike metal heads made about 700 years ago?

ghana.fact: In 1957, led by Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana became one of the first African countries south of the Sahara to win independence from European rule.
ghana.ask: Which country, led by Kwame Nkrumah, won independence in 1957?

liberia.fact: Liberia declared its independence in 1847, making it Africa's first republic to do so.
liberia.ask: Which country, in 1847, became the first African republic to declare its independence?

liberia.fact: In 2005 Liberia elected Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, the first woman elected to lead an African country.
liberia.ask: Which country elected Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, Africa's first elected woman president, in 2005?

guinea.fact: In 1958 Guinea became the first French colony in Africa to vote for full independence.
guinea.ask: Which country, in 1958, was the first French colony in Africa to vote for full independence?

senegal.fact: The African Renaissance Monument in Dakar, Senegal, finished in 2010, is the tallest statue in Africa at 49 meters.
senegal.ask: Which country's African Renaissance Monument, finished in 2010, is the tallest statue in Africa?

cabo-verde.fact: Cidade Velha in Cabo Verde, founded by the Portuguese in 1462, was the first European colonial town in the tropics.
cabo-verde.ask: Which island country's Cidade Velha was the first European colonial town in the tropics?

dr-congo.fact: The Ishango bone, a tally stick carved more than 20,000 years ago and possibly an early counting tool, was found in what is now the DR Congo.
dr-congo.ask: In which country was the Ishango bone found, a tally stick more than 20,000 years old?

gabon.fact: In 1913 Dr. Albert Schweitzer opened a jungle hospital at Lambaréné in Gabon. He later won the Nobel Peace Prize.
gabon.ask: In which country did Dr. Albert Schweitzer open his famous jungle hospital at Lambaréné in 1913?

sao-tome-and-principe.fact: The islands of São Tomé and Príncipe had no people living on them until Portuguese sailors arrived around 1470.
sao-tome-and-principe.ask: Which island country had no people at all until Portuguese sailors arrived around 1470?

angola.fact: Queen Nzinga ruled the kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba, in what is now Angola, in the 1600s and is remembered as a clever leader.
angola.ask: Which country remembers Queen Nzinga, who ruled the kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba in the 1600s?

ethiopia.fact: The ancient city of Aksum in Ethiopia is famous for its giant carved stone towers called stelae, made by the Kingdom of Aksum.
ethiopia.ask: Which country's ancient city of Aksum is famous for its giant carved stone towers, called stelae?

ethiopia.fact: Legend says a goat herder in Ethiopia named Kaldi discovered coffee after seeing his goats get lively from eating the berries.
ethiopia.ask: In which country does legend say a goat herder discovered coffee after his goats ate the berries?

somalia.fact: The Laas Geel caves in northern Somalia have colorful rock paintings of cattle and people that are thousands of years old.
somalia.ask: Which country's Laas Geel caves have colorful ancient paintings of cattle and people?

kenya.fact: Fort Jesus in Mombasa, Kenya, was built by the Portuguese in the 1590s to guard the harbor.
kenya.ask: Which country's Fort Jesus in Mombasa was built by the Portuguese in the 1590s?

kenya.fact: In 2004 Wangari Maathai of Kenya became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize, partly for her movement that planted millions of trees.
kenya.ask: Which country's Wangari Maathai won a Nobel Peace Prize in 2004 for her tree-planting movement?

tanzania.fact: Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania holds some of the oldest stone tools ever found, along with fossils of early humans.
tanzania.ask: Which country's Olduvai Gorge holds some of the oldest stone tools and early human fossils?

uganda.fact: In 1862 explorer John Hanning Speke found where the Nile River flows out of Lake Victoria, in what is now Uganda.
uganda.ask: In which country did explorer John Speke find where the Nile flows out of Lake Victoria in 1862?

madagascar.fact: Madagascar was first settled by sailors who came across the Indian Ocean from Borneo in Southeast Asia, more than 1,000 years ago.
madagascar.ask: Which island country was first settled by sailors who came all the way from Borneo?

seychelles.fact: The islands of Seychelles had no people living on them until French settlers arrived in 1770.
seychelles.ask: Which island country had no people living there until French settlers arrived in 1770?

malawi.fact: The Chongoni Rock Art Area in Malawi has one of the richest collections of rock paintings in Central Africa.
malawi.ask: Which country's Chongoni Rock Art Area has one of Central Africa's richest sets of rock paintings?

zambia.fact: Zambia, once called Northern Rhodesia, became independent in 1964 with Kenneth Kaunda as its first president.
zambia.ask: Which country, once called Northern Rhodesia, became independent in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda?

botswana.fact: The Tsodilo Hills in Botswana are full of ancient rock art and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2001.
botswana.ask: Which country's Tsodilo Hills, full of ancient rock paintings, became a World Heritage Site in 2001?

namibia.fact: Twyfelfontein in Namibia has more than 2,000 rock carvings of animals such as rhinos, elephants and giraffes, made over thousands of years.
namibia.ask: Which country's Twyfelfontein has more than 2,000 ancient rock carvings of animals?

south-africa.fact: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first Black president in 1994, after the country's first elections open to all races.
south-africa.ask: Which country elected Nelson Mandela as its president in 1994?

south-africa.fact: In 1967 Dr. Christiaan Barnard performed the world's first human heart transplant in Cape Town, South Africa.
south-africa.ask: In which country did Dr. Christiaan Barnard perform the first human heart transplant, in 1967?

south-africa.fact: Mapungubwe, in South Africa, was the center of a gold-trading kingdom about 800 years ago, where a famous small golden rhino was found.
south-africa.ask: Which country's Mapungubwe was a gold-trading kingdom where a little golden rhino was found?

lesotho.fact: King Moshoeshoe I founded the Basotho nation, now Lesotho, in the 1820s, using the flat-topped mountain of Thaba Bosiu as his stronghold.
lesotho.ask: Which mountain kingdom was founded by King Moshoeshoe I, with Thaba Bosiu as his stronghold?

zimbabwe.fact: The huge stone walls of the Great Enclosure at Great Zimbabwe, in Zimbabwe, were built without any mortar holding the stones together.
zimbabwe.ask: Which country's ancient Great Enclosure has huge stone walls built without any mortar?

benin.fact: The Royal Palaces of Abomey in Benin were built by the kings of Dahomey, a powerful West African kingdom, from the 1600s to the 1800s.
benin.ask: Which country's Royal Palaces of Abomey were built by the kings of Dahomey?

burkina-faso.fact: The Ruins of Loropéni in Burkina Faso are tall stone walls of an old settlement linked to the gold trade, and became the country's first World Heritage Site in 2009.
burkina-faso.ask: Which country's Ruins of Loropéni, tall old stone walls, became its first World Heritage Site in 2009?

mauritius.fact: The 1847 "Post Office" stamps of Mauritius are among the rarest and most valuable stamps in the world.
mauritius.ask: Which island country's 1847 "Post Office" stamps are among the rarest stamps in the world?
